plan.title: PROGENy pathway footprints in cytokine-stimulated bronchial epithelium
plan.analytical_narrative: The question asks which signaling pathways are ACTIVE in cytokine-stimulated versus vehicle-treated human bronchial epithelium, judged by the transcriptional footprint a pathway leaves rather than by which of its members are expressed. That maps directly onto the PROGENy footprint model estimated with decoupleR. The footprint needs a trustworthy per-gene statistic first, so the plan runs a grounded DESeq2 path on the 6-vs-6 unpaired, single-batch count matrix (12,000 genes x 12 samples, Salmon gene-level counts as delivered): blind-VST sample-structure QC (sample_01 is ~4x below the median library size — kept and inspected, not silently dropped), a minimal pre-filter, median-of-ratios size factors, a Wald test of cytokine-stimulated vs vehicle with an explicit reference level, apeglm shrinkage, and BH at alpha 0.05 with independent filtering. The full ranked Wald statistic of every tested gene (not a significant-genes list) then feeds the pathway-activity step: decoupleR mlm on the PROGENy human full model with the top 500 responsive genes per pathway, ulm as the second estimator, and per-sample pathway scores on the VST log matrix contrasted between groups with limma + BH. Membership-based enrichment (e.g. the staged WikiPathways human GMT) is deliberately NOT run — the question explicitly excludes judging activity by expressed pathway members. The Salmon import state is unknown, so the count model runs on the counts as delivered with no length offset and the plan says so; the length offset is lost and isoform-use changes can surface as DE. Small data: 12000x12 counts, low resources throughout.
